Finding the lands within the river fertile yet the people wasted and impoverished, Zao memorialized to open and dredge the ancient Qin Canal weir at Fangkou in Huai Prefecture; Forty thousand workers were employed, irrigating more than five thousand mou of farmland in Jiyuan, Henei, Wen, and Wuzhi.
71
七年十一月，入爲御史大夫。 造初赴鎭漢中，遇大雨，平地水深尺餘，乃禱鷄翁山祈晴，俄而疾風驅雲，即時開齊。 文宗嘗聞其事，會造入對言之，乃詔封鷄翁山爲侯。
In the eleventh month of the seventh year he returned to the capital as Censor-in-Chief. On his first journey to his post at Hanzhong, Zao was caught in heavy rain that left the flat ground more than a foot underwater. He prayed at Cock-Old-Man Mountain for clear weather, and soon a fierce wind drove off the clouds and the skies opened. Wenzong had heard of the incident; when Zao mentioned it during an audience, the emperor issued an edict ennobling Cock-Old-Man Mountain as a marquis.
72
九年五月，轉禮部尚書。 其年六月病卒，時年七十，贈右僕射。 有文集八十巻。 造於晩年積聚財貨，一無散施，時頗譏之。 子璋嗣。
In the fifth month of the ninth year he was transferred to Minister of Rites. He died of illness that sixth month, at the age of seventy, and was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat. He left collected works in eighty scrolls. In his later years Zao amassed wealth but gave nothing away, and many at the time mocked him for it. His son Zhang succeeded him.
73
璋以廕入仕，累佐使府，歴三郡刺史。 咸通末，爲徐泗節度使，徐州牙卒曰銀刀軍，頗驕橫。 璋至，誅其惡者五百餘人，自是軍中畏法。 入爲京兆尹，持法太深，豪右一皆屛跡。 會同昌公主薨，懿宗怒，殺醫官，其家屬宗枝下獄者三百人。 璋上疎切諫，以爲刑法太深。 帝怒，貶璋振州司馬。 制出，璋嘆曰：「生不逢時，死何足惜？」 是夜自縊而卒。
Zhang entered government through hereditary privilege, served repeatedly on commissioners' staffs, and governed three prefectures in succession. Late in the Xiantong reign he became military commissioner of Xu and Si, where the Xu Prefecture guards—the Silver Blade Army—were notoriously arrogant and domineering. On arrival Zhang executed more than five hundred of the worst offenders, and thereafter the army feared the law. He returned to the capital as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, where his stern enforcement of the law drove every powerful family into hiding. When Princess Tongchang died, Yizong in his rage executed the physicians and imprisoned three hundred of their kinsmen and clansmen. Zhang submitted a forceful memorial arguing that the punishments were too harsh. Enraged, the emperor demoted Zhang to staff administrator of Zhen Prefecture. When the edict was issued, Zhang sighed, "Born out of season—why regret death?" That night he hanged himself.
74
郭承嘏，字復卿。 曾祖尚父汾陽王。 祖晞，諸衞將軍。 父鈞。 承嘏生而秀異，乳保之年，即好筆硯。 比及成童，能通《五經》。 元和四年，禮部侍郎張弘靖知其才，擢升進士第，累辟使幕。 歴渭南尉。 入朝爲監察御史，遷起居舍人。 丁内艱，以孝聞，終喪，爲侍御史，職方、兵部二員外，兵部郎中。 太和六年，拜諫議大夫。 頻上疎，言時政得失。 文宗以鄭註爲太仆卿，承嘏論諫激切，註甚懼之。 本官知匭院事。 九年，轉給事中。
Guo Chenggu, styled Fuqing. His great-grandfather was the Prince of Fenyang, the Lord Father of the State. His grandfather Xi was a general of the imperial guards. His father was Jun. Chenggu was gifted from birth; even as a nursling he loved brush and inkstone. By boyhood he had mastered the Five Classics. In the fourth year of Yuanhe, Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Hongjing recognized his talent and advanced him to the jinshi degree; he served repeatedly on commissioners' staffs. He served as magistrate of Weinan. He entered court as investigating censor and was promoted to recorder of conduct. During mourning for his mother he was known for filial piety; after the mourning period he became attendant censor, then successively vice director in the Ministries of Appointments and War, and director in the Ministry of War. In the sixth year of Taihe he was appointed Remonstrance and Reviser. He repeatedly submitted memorials on the strengths and failings of current policy. When Wenzong appointed Zheng Zhu Director of the Imperial Stud, Chenggu remonstrated with fierce urgency, and Zhu was greatly afraid of him. In his regular post he also managed affairs of the Petition Box. In the ninth year he was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
75
開成元年，出爲華州刺史、兼御史中丞。 詔下，兩省叠詣中書，求承嘏出麾之由。 給事中盧載封還詔書，奏曰：「承嘏自居此官，繼有封駁，能奉其職，宜在瑣闥。 牧守之才，易爲推擇。」 文宗謂宰臣曰：「承嘏久在黃扉，欲優其祿俸，暫令廉問近關。 而諫列拜章，惜其稱職，甚美事也。」 乃復爲給事中。
In the first year of Kaicheng he was appointed prefect of Hua and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief. When the edict was issued, members of the two bureaus went repeatedly to the Secretariat to ask why Chenggu was being sent out of the capital. Supervising Secretary Lu Zai returned the sealed edict and memorialized, "Since Chenggu has held this office he has repeatedly drafted rejections and fulfilled his duties well; he should remain at court. A capable prefect is easy enough to find." Wenzong told the chancellors, "Chenggu has long served at court; I wished to improve his salary and briefly sent him to inspect a nearby pass. Yet the remonstrance officials submitted memorials, valuing his competence in office—a very fine thing indeed." He was then restored to Supervising Secretary.
76
文宗以淮南諸道累歳大旱，租賦不登，國用多闕。 及是，以度支、戸部分命宰臣鎭之。 承嘏論之曰：「宰相者，上調陰陽，下安黎庶，致君堯、舜，致時淸平。 俾之閲簿書，算緡帛，非所宜也。」 帝深嘉之，遷刑部侍郎。 時因朔望，以刑法官得對，文宗從容顧問，恩禮甚厚。 未及大用，以二年二月卒。 承嘏身歿之後，家無餘財，喪祭所費，皆親友共給而後具。 搢紳之流，無不痛惜。 贈吏部尚書。
Because the circuits south of the Huai had suffered great drought for successive years and taxes had gone uncollected, Wenzong found state revenues greatly short. At this time the ministries of revenue and household accounts were entrusted to chancellors to supervise. Chenggu argued, "Chancellors should harmonize yin and yang above and settle the common people below, bring the ruler to the level of Yao and Shun, and bring the age to clarity and peace. To have them examine ledgers and count strings of cash is not fitting." The emperor greatly approved and promoted him to Vice Minister of Justice. At that time, on the first and fifteenth of each month, judicial officials were permitted audience; Wenzong questioned him at leisure, and his favor and courtesy were very great. Before he could be greatly employed, he died in the second month of the second year. After Chenggu's death his household had no surplus wealth; burial and sacrifice expenses were all supplied by relatives and friends before they could be completed. The gentry grieved deeply. He was posthumously honored as Minister of Personnel.
77
殷侑，陳郡人。 父懌。 侑爲兒童時，勵志力學，不問家人資産。 及長，通經，以講習自娯。 貞元末，以《五經》登第，精於歴代沿革禮。 元和中，累爲太常博士。 時回紇請和親，朝廷計費五百萬緡。 朝廷方用兵伐叛，費用百端，欲緩其期。 乃命宗正少卿李孝誠奉使宣諭，以侑爲副。 侑謹重有節概，臨事俊辯。 既至虜庭，可汗初待漢使，盛陳兵甲，欲臣漢使而不答拜。 侑堅立不動，宣諭畢，可汗責其倨，宣言欲留而不遣。 行者皆懼，侑謂虜使曰：「可汗是漢家子婿，欲坐受使臣拜，是可汗失禮，非使臣之倨也。」 可汗憚其言，卒不敢逼。 使還，拜虞部員外郎。 王承宗拒命，遣侑銜命招諭之。 承宗尋稟朝旨，獻德、棣二州，遣二子入朝。 遷侑諫議大夫。 凡朝廷之得失，悉以陳論。 前後上八十四章，以言激切，出爲桂管觀察使。
Yin You was a man of Chen Commandery. His father was Yi. As a child You was determined to study hard and paid no heed to his family's property. When he grew up he mastered the classics and took lecturing and study as his pleasure. At the end of Zhenyuan he passed the examination in the Five Classics and was expert in the rites and institutions of successive dynasties. In Yuanhe he served repeatedly as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. At that time the Uighurs requested a marriage alliance, and the court calculated the cost at five million strings of cash. The court was then campaigning against rebels and expenses were manifold; it wished to delay the matter. It therefore appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan Li Xiaocheng to go as envoy to announce and instruct, with You as his deputy. You was careful, weighty, and possessed of integrity; in handling affairs he was sharp and eloquent. Once they reached the khan's court, the khan at first received the Han envoys with a great display of arms and armor, intending to make them bow without returning the courtesy. You stood firm without moving; when the announcement was finished the khan reproached his arrogance and declared he intended to detain them and not send them back. The travelers were all afraid; You told the barbarian envoy, "The khan is the Han emperor's son-in-law; if he wishes to sit and receive the envoy's bow, it is the khan who has lost propriety, not the envoy's arrogance." The khan feared his words and in the end did not dare compel him. On returning from the mission he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Parks. Wang Chengzong defied orders; You was sent bearing imperial command to summon and instruct him. Chengzong soon submitted to court instructions, presented De and Di prefectures, and sent two sons to court. You was promoted to Remonstrance and Reviser. Whatever gains or losses the court suffered, he set them all forth in discussion. In all he submitted eighty-four memorials; because his words were fierce and urgent he was sent out as supervisory commissioner of the Gui circuit.
78
寶暦元年，檢校右散騎常侍、洪州刺史，轉江西觀察使。 所至以潔廉著稱。 入爲衞尉卿。 文宗初即位，滄州李同捷叛，而王廷湊助逆，欲加兵鎭州，詔五品已上都省集議。 時上鋭於破賊，宰臣莫敢異議。 獨侑以廷湊再亂河朔，方徇招懷，雖附兇徒，未甚彰露，宜且含容，專討同捷。 其疎末云：「伏願以宗社安危爲大計，以善師攻心爲神武，以含垢安人爲遠圖，以網漏呑舟爲至誡。」 文宗雖不納，深所嘉之。
In the first year of Baoli he was made acting Right Regular Palace Attendant and prefect of Hong, then transferred to supervisory commissioner of the Jiangxi circuit. Wherever he went he was known for purity and integrity. He returned to the capital as Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud. When Wenzong first took the throne, Li Tongjie of Cang Prefecture rebelled while Wang Tingcou aided the rebellion; the court wished to send troops against Zhen Prefecture and ordered all officials of the fifth rank and above in the central ministries to assemble for deliberation. At that time the emperor was eager to crush the rebels, and no chancellor dared dissent. Only You held that Tingcou had twice thrown the Hebei region into turmoil; the court was then pursuing appeasement, and though he had joined the violent faction his offense was not yet fully exposed—he should for the time being be tolerated while the court concentrated on Tongjie. At the end of his memorial he wrote, "I humbly hope Your Majesty will take the security of the altars of state as the great plan, take winning hearts by a good army as divine martial prowess, take bearing grime to settle the people as far-reaching design, and take letting the net leak so great boats pass as the highest caution." Wenzong did not adopt it, but greatly approved of it.
79
滄景平，以侑嘗爲滄州行軍司馬。 太和四年，加檢校工部尚書、滄齊德觀察使。 時大兵之後，滿目荊榛，遺骸蔽野，寂無人煙。 侑不以妻子之官，始至，空城而已。 侑攻苦食淡，與士卒同勞苦。 周歳之後，流民繈負而歸。 侑上表請借耕牛三萬，以給流民，乃詔度支賜綾絹五萬匹，買牛以給之。 數年之後，戸口滋饒，倉稟盈積，人皆忘亡。 初州兵三萬，悉取給於度支。 侑一歳而賦入自贍其半，二歳而給用悉周，請罷度支給賜。 而勸課多方，民吏胥悅，上表請立德政碑。 以功加檢校吏部尚書。 侑以郭下淸池縣在子城北，非便，奏移於南郭之内。
When Cang and Jing were pacified, because You had once served as acting military administrator of Cang Prefecture. In the fourth year of Taihe he was made acting Minister of Works and supervisory commissioner of the Cang, Qi, and De circuit. At that time, after great military campaigns, thorns and brambles filled the landscape, abandoned corpses covered the wilds, and the land lay silent and deserted. You did not bring his wife and children to his post; when he first arrived there was only an empty city. You ate sparingly and labored bitterly, sharing hardship with the soldiers. After a full year, displaced people returned carrying their children on their backs. You submitted a memorial requesting to borrow thirty thousand plow oxen to supply the displaced people; an edict was then issued for the Ministry of Revenue to grant fifty thousand bolts of silk and damask to buy oxen and distribute them. After several years households multiplied and storehouses overflowed; people forgot exile and death. At first the prefectural army numbered thirty thousand, all supplied by the Ministry of Revenue. In one year You's tax revenues supported half of them; in two years supplies were fully covered, and he requested that Ministry of Revenue grants be ended. He also encouraged agriculture in many ways; officials and clerks were all pleased, and he submitted a memorial requesting a stele of virtuous governance. For his achievement he was made acting Minister of Personnel. You held that Qingchi County under the prefectural seat lay north of the inner city and was inconvenient; he memorialized to move it within the southern wall.
80
六年，入爲刑部尚書，尋復檢校吏部尚書、鄆州刺史、兼御史大夫，充天平軍節度、鄆曹濮觀察等使。 自元和末，收復師道十二州爲三鎭。 朝廷務安反側，征賦所入，盡留贍軍，貫緡尺帛，不入王府。 侑以軍賦有餘，賦不上供，非法也，乃上表起太和七年，請歳供兩稅、榷酒等錢十五萬貫、粟五萬碩。 詔曰：「鄆、曹、濮等州，元和已來，地本殷實，自分三道，十五餘年，雖頒詔書，竟未入賦。 殷侑承兵戈之後，當歉旱之餘，勤力奉公，謹身守法。 才及周歳，已致阜安。 而又體國輸忠，率先入貢，成三軍奉上之志，陳一境樂輸之心。 尋有表章，良用嘉嘆！」 尋就加檢校右僕射。
In the sixth year he returned to the capital as Minister of Justice, then again became acting Minister of Personnel, prefect of Yan, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, serving as military commissioner of the Tianping Army and supervisory commissioner of Yan, Cao, and Pu. From the end of Yuanhe, when the twelve prefectures of Shidao were recovered they became three commands. The court sought to settle those who had turned against it; all tax revenues collected were retained to support the army—strings of cash and bolts of cloth and silk did not enter the imperial treasury. You held that since military levies had a surplus and taxes were not submitted upward, this was unlawful; he therefore submitted a memorial beginning with the seventh year of Taihe, requesting annual submission of fifteen thousand strings of the two taxes and monopoly wine revenues, and fifty thousand shi of grain. An edict read, "The prefectures of Yan, Cao, and Pu, since Yuanhe, were originally prosperous lands; since they were divided into three commands, more than fifteen years have passed; though edicts were repeatedly issued, taxes were never submitted. Yin You, after the warfare, amid famine and drought, labored diligently in service to the state and kept himself careful and law-abiding. In barely a full year he already brought prosperity and peace. Moreover he embodied the state's loyalty, took the lead in submitting tribute, fulfilled the three armies' intent to serve the throne, and expressed the whole circuit's willingness to contribute. Soon afterward he submitted another memorial—truly worthy of praise and admiration!" He was then promptly made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
81
九年，御史大夫温造劾侑不由制旨，增監軍俸入，賦斂於人。 上不問，以庾承宣代還。
In the ninth year Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao impeached You for increasing the army supervisor's salary income without following the prescribed edict and levying taxes on the people. The emperor did not inquire into it and sent Yu Chengxuan to replace him and return.
82
其年，濮州録事參軍崔元武，於五縣人吏率斂，及縣官料錢，以私馬擡估納官，計絹一百二十匹。 大理寺斷三犯倶發，以重者論。 只以中私馬爲重，止令削三任官。 而刑部覆奏，令決杖配流。 獄未決。 侑奏曰：「法官不習法律，三犯不同，即坐其所重。 元武所犯，皆枉法取受，準律，枉法十五匹已上絞。 《律疎》云：即以贓致罪，頻犯者並累科。 據元武所犯，令當入處絞刑。」 疎奏，元武依刑部奏，決六十，流賀州。 乃授侑刑部尚書。 八月，檢校右僕射，復爲天平軍節度使。 上以温造所奏深文故也。
That year, Pu Prefecture recorder Cui Yuanwu, among the clerks and officials of five counties, collected levies and official stipend money, used a private horse to inflate the valuation and submit it to the government, totaling one hundred twenty bolts of silk. The Court of Judicial Review ruled on three offenses committed together and judged by the most serious. They took only the private horse offense as the serious one and merely ordered removal from three ranks of office. But the Ministry of Justice on review memorialized ordering beating with the staff and banishment. The case was not yet decided. You memorialized, "The judges do not understand the law; when three offenses differ, they should be punished for the most serious. All of Yuanwu's offenses were wrongful taking and receipt; according to the code, wrongful taking of fifteen bolts or more warrants strangulation. The Statutes Commentary states: when crimes are caused by illicit goods and offenses are repeatedly committed, punishments are cumulated. According to Yuanwu's offenses, he should receive strangulation." When the memorial was submitted, Yuanwu was decided according to the Ministry of Justice memorial: sixty blows with the staff and banishment to He Prefecture. You was then appointed Minister of Justice. In the eighth month he was made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and again became military commissioner of the Tianping Army. The emperor did this because of the harsh legalism in Wen Zao's impeachment.
83
開成元年，復召爲刑部尚書。 時初經李訓之亂，上問侑治安之術。 侑極言委任責成，宜在朝之耆德，新進小生，無宜輕用。 帝深嘉之，賜錦彩三百匹。 及中謝，又令中使就第賜金十斤。 其年七月，檢校左僕射，出爲襄州刺史、山南東道節度使。
In the first year of Kaicheng he was again summoned as Minister of Justice. At that time, having just passed through the turmoil of Li Xun, the emperor asked You about the art of securing peace. You spoke forcefully of entrusting responsibility and demanding results; the court should rely on elders of virtue, and newly advanced young men should not be lightly employed. The emperor greatly approved and bestowed three hundred bolts of brocade and silk. At his audience of thanks he was again ordered by palace envoy to his residence to bestow ten jin of gold. In the seventh month of that year he was made acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and went out as prefect of Xiang and military commissioner of the Shannan East circuit.
84
二年三月，以病求代，以太子賓客分司東都。 十一月，復檢校右僕射，出爲忠武節度、陳許蔡觀察等使。 三年七月，卒於鎭，時年七十二，贈司空。
In the third month of the second year he requested replacement on account of illness and was made Crown Prince's Mentor with duty at the Eastern Capital. In the eleventh month he was again made acting Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and went out as military commissioner of Zhongwu and supervisory commissioner of Chen, Xu, and Cai. In the seventh month of the third year he died at his post, at age seventy-two, and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works.
85
侑以通經入仕，觀風撫俗，所蒞有聲。 而晩年急於大用，稍通權幸，物望減於往時。 子羽。
You entered service through mastery of the classics; in observing customs and settling the people, wherever he served he had a reputation. But in his later years he was eager for great employment and gradually cultivated connections with the powerful; public esteem fell short of earlier times. His son was Yu.
86
羽太和五年登進士第，籓府辟召，不至通顯。 子盈孫。
Yu passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Taihe; he was recruited to commissioners' staffs but never rose to prominence. His son was Yingsun.
87
盈孫，乾符末爲成都掾。 駕在西川，用爲太常博士，禮學有祖風。 光啓二年冬，隨駕自成都還。 三年二月，駐蹕鳳翔。 時宗廟爲賊所焚，車駕至京，告享無所。 四月，盈孫謂宰執曰：「太廟十一室，並祧廟八室，及三太后三室，因光啓元年十二月二十五日車駕出宮，其縁室法物神主，本司載行，至鄠縣並被盜剽奪。 皇帝還宮，合先制造。」 宰相鄭延昌奏曰：「太廟大殿二十二間，功績至大，計料支費不少； 兼宗廟制度，損益重難，今未審依元料修奉，爲復別有商量。」 敕付禮院詳議。
Yingsun, at the end of the Qianfu reign, was an aide in Chengdu. When the emperor was in western Shu he was employed as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; in ritual learning he had his family's style. In the winter of the second year of Guangqi he followed the emperor back from Chengdu. In the second month of the third year the imperial carriage halted at Fengxiang. At that time the imperial ancestral temple had been burned by rebels; when the imperial carriage reached the capital there was nowhere to announce the sacrifices. In the fourth month Yingsun told the chief ministers, "The main temple has eleven chambers, together with eight chambers of the disestablished temple, and three chambers for the three empresses—a total of twenty-two. Because on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the first year of Guangqi, when the imperial carriage left the palace, the ritual objects and spirit tablets of those chambers that the office was to transport were all looted at Hu County. Now that the emperor has returned to the palace, they should first be remade." Chancellor Zheng Yanchang memorialized, "The main hall of the imperial ancestral temple has twenty-two bays; the materials and expenses are very great; and the temple institutions, whether to reduce or increase, are weighty and difficult. It is not yet clear whether to repair according to the original specifications or to deliberate otherwise." An edict entrusted the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for detailed deliberation.
88
時博士四人，杜用勵在利州，崔澄在河中，封舜卿在巴南。 獨盈孫獻議曰：「太廟制度。 歴代參詳，皆符典經，難議損益。 謹按舊制，十一室，二十三間，十一架。 垣墉廣袤之度，堂室淺深之規，階陛等級之差，棟宇崇低之則，前古所謂奢不能侈，儉不能逾者也。 今以朝廷帑藏方虚，費用稍廣，須資變禮，將務從宜，固不可易前聖之規模，狹大朝之制度，當憑典實，別有參詳。 謹按至德二年，以太廟方修，新作神主，於長安殿安置，便行饗告之禮，如同宗廟之儀，以俟廟成，方爲遷祔。 當時議論，無所是非。 竊知今者京城除大内正衙外，別無殿宇。 伏聞先有詔旨，且以少府監大廳權充太廟。 伏縁十一室於五間之中，陳設隘狹，伏請接續廳之兩頭，成十一室，薦饗之。 三太后廟，即於監内西南，別取屋宇三間，且充廟室。 候太廟修奉畢日，別議遷祔。」 敕旨依奏。 其神主、法物、樂懸，皆盈孫奏重修制，知禮者稱爲博洽。
At that time there were four erudites: Du Yongli was in Li Prefecture, Cui Cheng in Hezhong, and Feng Shunqing in Banan. Only Yingsun submitted an opinion: "On the institutions of the imperial ancestral temple, successive dynasties have examined them in detail; all accord with canonical standards, and reduction or increase is difficult to discuss. I respectfully examine the old institutions: eleven chambers, twenty-three bays, eleven frames. The breadth and length of the enclosing walls, the depth and shallowness of the halls and chambers, the gradations of steps and stairs, the standards of height and loftiness of the beams and rafters—all these are what the ancients called that extravagance cannot exceed and frugality cannot fall below. Now the court treasury is empty and expenses somewhat broad; we must rely on altered rites and strive for what is fitting—but we cannot change the former sage's scale or narrow the great court's institutions; we should rely on canonical fact and deliberate separately. I respectfully note that in the second year of Zhide, because the imperial ancestral temple was under repair, new spirit tablets were made and placed in Chang'an Hall, and the offering and announcement rites were performed as in the ancestral temple, to await completion of the temple before transfer and enshrinement. At that time in discussion there was no dispute. I know that at present in the capital, apart from the inner palace and main audience hall, there are no other halls. I have heard there was already an edict temporarily using the great hall of the Palace Directorate as the imperial ancestral temple. Because eleven chambers within five bays are cramped for arrangement, I humbly request extending the two ends of the adjoining hall to form eleven chambers for offerings. For the temple of the three empresses, take three rooms in the southwest of the directorate and temporarily use them as temple chambers. When repair of the imperial ancestral temple is completed, transfer and enshrinement may be discussed separately." An edict approved the memorial. The spirit tablets, ritual objects, and musical instruments were all remade on Yingsun's memorial; those who understood ritual praised his breadth of learning.
89
龍紀元年十一月，昭宗郊祀圓丘。 兩中尉楊復恭及兩樞密，皆請朝服。 盈孫上疎曰：「臣昨赴齋宮，見中尉、樞密内臣，皆具朝服。 臣尋前代及國朝典令，無内官朝服制度。 伏以皇帝陛下，承天御暦，聖祚中興，祗見宗祧，克陳大禮，皆稟髙祖、太宗之成制，必循虞、夏、商、周之舊經。 軒冕服章，式遵彜憲。 若内官要衣朝服，令依所守官本品之服。 事雖無據，粗可行之。 臣忝禮司，合具陳奏。」 時中貴皆如宰相大臣朝服，故盈孫論之。 帝雖不從，嘉其所守。 轉秘書少監，卒。
In the eleventh month of the first year of Longji, Zhaozong performed the suburban sacrifice at the Round Mound. Both army supervisors Yang Fugong and the two privy secretaries all requested court robes. Yingsun submitted a memorial, "Yesterday when I went to the fasting palace I saw the army supervisors and privy secretaries, all inner officials, fully equipped in court robes. I have examined former dynasties and our court's statutes and orders; there is no institution of court robes for inner officials. I humbly consider that the emperor, receiving Heaven's mandate and governing the era, with the sacred reign in restoration, has reverently appeared before the ancestral temple and can perform the great rites—all following the completed institutions of Gaozu and Taizong, and necessarily following the old canons of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou. Carriages, caps, robes, and insignia should follow canonical law. If inner officials must wear court robes, let them wear the robes of the official rank they hold. Though the matter lacks precedent, it may roughly be done. I, who am charged with ritual affairs, should set it forth in full." At that time the powerful inner officials all wore court robes like chancellors and great ministers; therefore Yingsun argued against it. Though the emperor did not follow it, he approved his integrity. He was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and died.
90
徐晦，進士擢第，登直言極諫制科，授櫟陽尉，皆自楊憑所薦。 及憑得罪，貶臨賀尉，交親無敢祖送者； 獨晦送至藍田，與憑言別。 時故相權德輿與憑交分最深，知晦之行，因謂晦曰：「今日送臨賀，誠爲厚矣，無乃爲累乎！」 晦曰：「晦自布衣受楊公之眷，方茲流播，爭忍無言而別？ 如他日相公爲奸邪所譖，失意於外，晦安得與相公輕別？」 德輿嘉其眞懇，大稱之於朝。 不數日，御史中丞李夷簡請爲監察，晦白夷簡曰：「生平不踐公門，公何取信而見獎拔？」 夷簡曰：「聞君送楊臨賀，不顧犯難，肯負國乎？」 由是知名。 歴殿中侍御史、尚書郎，出爲晉州刺史。 入拜中書舍人。 寶暦元年，出爲福建觀察使。 二年，入爲工部侍郎，出爲同州刺史、兼御史中丞。 太和四年，征拜兵部侍郎。 五年，爲太子賓客，分司東都。 晦性強直，不隨世態，當官守正。 唯嗜酒太過，晩年喪明，乃至沈廢。 以禮部尚書致仕。 開成三年三月卒，贈兵部尚書。
Xu Hui passed the jinshi examination, passed the direct-criticism examination, and was appointed magistrate of Liyang—all through Yang Ping's recommendation. When Ping was found guilty and demoted to magistrate of Linhe, none of his relatives and friends dared escort him on his way; only Hui escorted him as far as Lantian and spoke his farewell with Ping. At that time the former chancellor Quan Deyu, who had the deepest ties with Ping, knowing of Hui's journey, therefore told Hui, "Today in escorting the Linhe magistrate you have indeed shown great depth—but will it not become a burden?" Hui replied, "Hui, from commoner status, received Lord Yang's favor; now that he is cast into exile, how could I bear to part without a word? If someday, Lord Chancellor, you are slandered by the wicked and lose favor outside the capital, how could Hui lightly part from the Lord Chancellor?" Deyu admired his sincerity and praised him greatly at court. Within a few days Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian requested him as investigating censor; Hui told Yijian, "All my life I have not crossed the gates of great officials—why do you trust and reward me with promotion?" Yijian replied, "I heard that you escorted Yang the Linhe magistrate, not fearing offense and willing to bear the state's burden—is that not so?" From this he became known. He served successively as attendant censor and director in the Secretariat, and went out as prefect of Jin. He entered court as Secretariat Drafter. In the first year of Baoli he went out as supervisory commissioner of Fujian. In the second year he returned to the capital as Vice Minister of Works, then went out as prefect of Tong and concurrent Vice Censor-in-Chief. In the fourth year of Taihe he was summoned as Vice Minister of War. In the fifth year he became Crown Prince's Mentor with duty at the Eastern Capital. Hui's nature was forceful and upright; he did not follow the ways of the age and in office upheld rectitude. Only he loved wine too much; in his later years he lost his sight and was reduced to utter incapacity. He retired as Minister of Rites. In the third month of the third year of Kaicheng he died; posthumously honored as Vice Minister of War.
91
史臣曰：温、柳二公，以文行飾躬，砥礪名節，當官守法，侃侃有大臣之節，而竟不登三事，位止正卿。 所以知公輔之量，以和爲貴。 漢武帝畏汲黯而相孫弘，太宗重魏徴而委玄齡，其旨遠也。 韋、崔名士，薦賢致主，綽有古風。 殷司空治民，斯爲循吏，而忠規壯節，至晩不衰。 徐、郭讜言，郁爲佳士。 如數君者，實爲令人。
The historian remarks: The two lords Wen and Liu, adorning themselves with literary conduct, honing their name and integrity, upholding the law in office, were earnest and possessed the integrity of great ministers—yet in the end they did not ascend to the Three Dukes and stopped at regular third rank. From this one knows that the measure of chief minister values harmony. Emperor Wu of Han feared Ji An yet made Sun Hong chancellor; Taizong valued Wei Zheng yet entrusted Xuanling—how far-reaching the intent! Wei and Cui were famous scholars who recommended the worthy to serve the ruler; they had abundant ancient style. Minister of Works Yin in governing the people was a model circumspect official, yet his loyal remonstrance and stalwart integrity did not fade even in old age. Xu and Guo's forthright words were rich and formed excellent scholars. Men such as these several lords were truly admirable.
92
贊曰：柳氏禮法，公忠節概。 搏撃爲優，彌綸則隘。 夏卿獎拔，晦叔匡將。 徐、郭之議，金玉鏘鏘。
Praise runs: The Liu family's ritual law, public loyalty and stalwart integrity. Striking blows was their strength; weaving governance was their limit. Xiaqing rewarded and elevated; Huishu supported and guided. The remonstrance of Xu and Guo—gold and jade, ringing clear.
